title: Diana Flores Is Opening Doors for a New Generation of Women Flag Footballers
summary: The newly signed Nike athlete reflects on perseverance, leadership and the lessons that have shaped her journey from a young girl fighting for a place on the field to one of the sport’s most recognizable stars.
body_markdown:
**When**[Diana Flores](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-signs-two-time-world-champion-diana-flores-growing-its-flag-football-roster) **first stepped onto a flag football field at age 8, the sport was still worlds away from the Olympic stage. Growing up in Mexico City, she played in oversize boys’ jerseys on makeshift fields, far from the bright lights and roaring crowds of major stadiums. With few structural resources, little recognition and no clear path to a future in the sport, she learned early that pursuing her passion often meant finding ways around obstacles. Today, Flores is among the most influential figures in flag football. As captain and quarterback of Mexico’s national team, she has helped lead her country to two World Games gold medals and become a global ambassador as the sport prepares to make its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028. Now, she’s marking another milestone in her career, joining the Nike family as the brand’s newest flag football athlete. What began as a childhood passion has grown into a career that has helped change the possibilities for women and girls in football. For Flores, winning has come to mean more than championships. The same determination that carried her through those early years now drives her efforts to expand access to the sport and create opportunities for the next generation. And while her competitive fire remains as strong as ever, her understanding of success has evolved beyond the scoreboard. Here, she reflects on perseverance, leadership and the lessons that have shaped her journey from a young girl fighting for a place on the field to one of the sport’s most recognizable stars.**


**The very first time that I stepped on the football field, I saw the passion of all the girls who were playing the game.** They were being loud. They were being strong. They were so empowered. That feeling of empowerment is what made me fall in love with football back then, and it’s what keeps me falling in love with the game today.


**When I was young, there were lots of things I felt I couldn’t question.** “You’re not allowed to step on the football field.” “You have to clear another space if you want to play.” That’s just the way it was back then. So I’d do it. I’d just say, “Okay, if I have to clear a space to play, I’m going to do it. If I have to wear men’s jerseys and adjust them right before the game, I’ll do that.” Whatever it was going to take to play the game, I was going to do it.


> “Every time I step onto the field, I’m still that same 8-year-old girl. I’m just as passionate. The field is my safe place, even today.”
>
>
> Diana Flores, two-time flag football World Games gold medalist


**I was determined to keep going and doing what I loved, and that helped me build the mindset to overcome all of the no’s we heard.** Instead of looking at the challenges we had, I learned to look at my strengths and ask, “How can I make this happen?” That’s the biggest lesson that my journey has taught me — that passion, love and commitment can beat anything that life throws your way.


**To see how far women have come from those early days makes me feel incredibly proud.** We had to fight so hard to have a space, to have recognition, to have that feeling of belonging. When I look at all the opportunities available to girls and women in football now, and everything that’s still to come, I feel so excited about the future.


**Every time I step onto the field, I’m still that same 8-year-old girl.** I’m just as passionate. In that moment, I don’t care about anything happening anywhere else. All I care about is catching the ball, throwing the ball and celebrating with my teammates. That’s all that matters. The field is my safe place, even today.


**One of the things I love most about playing quarterback is the constant process of discovery and challenge.** My position requires a lot of decision-making and learning how to connect with my teammates in so many different ways. Football has helped me discover who I am, not only as an athlete, but as a leader. It’s taught me to be perseverant, disciplined and passionate in everything I do. That magic of teamwork is part of what makes flag football so special.


**I put myself in high-pressure situations before they happen.** I do a lot of visualization. If we’re down by a touchdown with only 20 seconds left on the clock, I’ve already lived that moment in my head. So when I find myself in that situation in real life, it’s not as scary. My brain processes what’s happening differently. Instead of panicking, I can focus on executing the next play and ask myself, “How can I solve this?”


**I’m super demanding of myself in everything I do.** Whether it’s my training or something in my life off the field, I expect a lot from myself. Every day brings a new challenge, and sometimes those expectations can be difficult to balance.


> “I put myself in high-pressure situations before they happen. I do a lot of visualization. If we’re down by a touchdown with only 20 seconds left on the clock, I’ve already lived that moment in my head. So when I find myself in that situation in real life, it’s not as scary.”
>
>
> Diana Flores


**As an athlete, I am competitive.** I have a winning mindset. I want to win, win everything, all the time. I take seriously the responsibility of bringing my country, my team and my people to the biggest stages. But my understanding of the game has evolved over the years to go beyond just winning medals. I’ve realized that the game is about more than just the result. It’s about reminding people what we’re all capable of. That dreams come true. That we all belong. That by just doing your best and showing up, you make other people feel seen and heard, and that is life-changing.


**Knowing I have a solid team behind me takes a lot of weight off my shoulders.** I trust my teammates and coaches to make the best decisions, even under pressure, and that allows me to focus on doing my part. But they've also helped me grow as a leader and a person. We're all fighting our own fights, and seeing my teammates show up every day — being brave and giving their best no matter what they’re going through — inspires me. They’ve taught me to be more empathetic, to see things through other people’s eyes, and to recognize where I can continue to grow.


**The sisterhood we’ve built on the national team has been everything to me.** We’ve lived through amazing moments together — gold medals, championships, so many victories. The cheering every time we make a good play, every time we overcome a challenge together. I still get goosebumps thinking about those moments. Those are the little things I carry in my heart.


**It means a lot to me to start this new chapter with Nike, especially at this moment in my career and in the sport.** I think about growing up in Mexico, one of my first pairs of cleats were Nikes. I dreamed about having all the cool gear and opportunities that other athletes had. To look back on those days and see where I am now, it’s incredible.


> “My understanding of the game has evolved over the years to go beyond just winning medals. t’s about reminding people what we’re all capable of. That by just doing your best and showing up, you make other people feel seen and heard, and that is life-changing.”
>
>
> Diana Flores


**With this partnership, we’re going to be able to join forces to continue pushing this sport forward.** I want to keep making the game more accessible for girls around the world, so it no longer feels like a dream that’s far away, but something within reach. It’s about opening doors, creating opportunities and changing lives.


**Don’t let the challenges make you feel less, or make you feel that you don’t belong, because you do.** Sometimes the path might be longer for us, and that’s part of life. But you have the power to change that narrative, and it starts by changing the narrative for yourself.


**There’s a saying in Spanish that I’ve carried with me since I was very young: “Para tener éxito, no hay que perder el enfoque.”** It means, *To be successful, you can’t lose focus.* I don’t even remember how I started saying it, but focus has always been a big part of my life. I truly believe that what you keep putting in your mind every day becomes your reality and helps create the path toward your biggest goals.


- [For The Win](https://about.nike.com/en/topics/for-the-win)
